- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.27) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment or negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.10) — particularly when recent prices are trending down — and shift forecast upward to avoid missing rebounds.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day window if sentiment is weak or mixed — prices often rebound later.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but prices are flat or slightly declining, expect a mean-reversion correction in the next 5–10 days — reduce forecast slope.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >80.00) are common — cap forecasts at +5–10% above peak unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.18–0.36), use a 3–5 day smoothing filter to avoid erratic forecast swings.
- If true outcome is consistently 2–3% higher than forecast in the last 3–5 days of the 30d window, apply a 1–2% upward bias correction for the next forecast.
